stem:
Marble chips or calcium carbonate react with hydrochloric acid as:

\(\text{CaCO}_3 + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{CaCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2\)

The reaction is carried out twice and the following graphs were obtained.

(The figure plots Volume of \(\text{CO}_2\) (in cm\(^3\)) on the y-axis against Time (min) on the x-axis. Two curves rise and level off at the SAME final volume: "Experiment II" rises more steeply and reaches the plateau first; "Experiment I" rises more slowly and reaches the same plateau later.)

Which of the following statements is incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: Reaction is faster in experiment II.

options.label: B
options.text: Same amount of marble chips and hydrochloric acid is used for both the experiments.

options.label: C
options.text: Marble chips taken in experiment II are smaller in size than the marble chips taken in experiment I.

stem:
Observe the given figure carefully. Which of the following observation(s) is/are correct?

(The figure shows lead nitrate crystals in a dry test tube being held by a test tube holder and heated over a burner. Labels: "Test tube holder", "Dry test tube", "Lead nitrate crystals", "Burner".)

1. A double decomposition reaction takes place.
2. Brown fumes of \(\text{NO}_2\) are evolved.
3. Red residue is left behind in the test tube.

stem:
The emission of brown fumes in the given experimental set-up is due to

(The figure shows a test tube containing lead nitrate held at an angle and heated over a burner; brown fumes rise from the mouth of the test tube. Labels: "Brown fumes", "Lead nitrate", "Burner".)

options.label: A
options.text: thermal decomposition of lead nitrate which produces brown fumes of nitrogen dioxide.

options.label: B
options.text: thermal decomposition of lead nitrate which produces brown fumes of lead oxide.

options.label: C
options.text: oxidation of lead nitrate forming lead oxide and oxygen.

options.label: D
options.text: oxidation of lead nitrate forming lead oxide and nitrogen dioxide.
